## Synthesizing Clinical Neurobiology and Statistical Representation Learning

The empirical results across `ADNI-MCI`, `TCGA-BRCA`, `TCGA-KIRC`, and the synthetic ground-truth benchmarks demonstrate that predictive accuracy and mechanistic localization do not need to be traded against one another when multi-view integration is organized around an explicit linear entrypoint ($\mathbf{Z}_{m,\text{lin}} = \mathbf{X}_m \mathbf{V}_m$). For the clinical neuroscientist or neuropsychologist, the primary value of `SiMR` lies in how cross-modal supervision shapes the learned anatomical basis. When structural MRI is decomposed in isolation via `PCA`, every one of the $62$ DKT parcels loads on every axis, and the result explains $R^2 =$ `{python} N.adni_pca` of composite cognitive severity (`CogPC1`), falling to `{python} N.adni_pca_rf` under single-axis decision tree splits. Coupling structural MRI views to an 11-scale cognitive battery during training (`Protocol B`) with non-negative approximate Stiefel regularization (`nsa_flow`, $w = 0.50, q = 0.85$) concentrates the held-out prediction in one component per view (vol/area $R^2 =$ `{python} N.attr_va_best_r2` alone), whose replicated features are entorhinal, temporal-lobe and inferior parietal measures (@fig-adni-neuroanatomy-flagship). Whether this pattern corresponds to stages of neurofibrillary pathology [@braak1991neuropathological; @dickerson2009cortical; @jack2018nia] is not tested here. On DiReCT cortical thickness one consensus component tracks a global factor (`{python} N.attr_dkt_pc1` of the variance), and its regional basis replicates only when the collapse penalty is turned off (`collapse_weight = 0`).

For the machine learning researcher, our four-probe evaluation resolves why post-hoc rotation or unmixing steps (`ICA` [@hyvarinen2000independent], orthogonal Procrustes rotations [@schonemann1966generalized], or dense SVD factors) often appear competitive under ridge regression yet fail when individual coordinates are inspected or thresholded. Because $\operatorname{span}(\mathbf{X}_m \mathbf{V}_m \mathbf{M}) = \operatorname{span}(\mathbf{X}_m \mathbf{V}_m)$ for any invertible $\mathbf{M} \in \mathrm{GL}(k)$, linear subspace probes measure only aggregate subspace capacity. Pairing linear subspace probes with coordinate-aligned Random Forest probes (`RF(XV)`) and ground-truth support recovery ($F_1$) exposes diagonal coordinate mixing directly: across all `{python} N.n_blocks` benchmarks, the Random Forest minus linear score is `{python} N.drop_pca` for `PCA`, against `{python} N.drop_best_models` for the models with the smallest drop, and support recovery on the $50\%$-sparse `Linear` regime ranges from $F_1 =$ `{python} N.f1_linear_q05_min` to `{python} N.f1_linear_q05_max`.

## Practical Method and Operating-Point Selection Guide

To translate these findings into actionable guidance for new multi-modal studies, @tbl-practitioner-guide maps common biomedical study designs to the recommended `SiMR` solver and quantile sparsity operating point $q$.

| Biomedical Scenario & Modality Regime | Recommended Architecture | Recommended `nsa_flow` Operating Point | Empirical & Mathematical Rationale |
|:--------------|:---------------------------------|:---------------------------------|:---------------------------|
| Multi-View Clinical Translation (e.g., training on MRI + Cognition, deploying on MRI alone; $N \sim 10^3$) | `LEND` or `Flow-SiMR-V` | $w = 0.50$, $q = 0.50$ (discovery) or $q = 0.85$ (focal) | On `ADNI-MCI` MRI-only cognitive prediction the best 3-seed linear score is `{python} N.adni_best_r2` (`{python} N.adni_best_model`) and the best single-axis score `{python} N.adni_rf_best` (`{python} N.adni_rf_best_model`); at $q = 0.85$ one component carries the prediction; on views dominated by a global factor set `collapse_weight = 0` before reading regional loadings. |
| High-Dimensional Multi-Omics Pathway Discovery (e.g., mRNA + CNV + RPPA; $p_m \gg N$) | `SiMLR` or `Flow-SiMR-V` | $w = 0.50$, $q = 0.50$, `positivity="positive"` | `TCGA-BRCA` accuracy `{python} N.brca_SiMLR` (`SiMLR`); support recovery on `NonnegParts` $F_1 =$ `{python} N.f1_simlr_np`. |
| Minimal Diagnostic Assay / Targeted Biomarker Panel Design | `SiMLR` | $w = 0.50$, $q = 0.80$–$0.85$, `positivity="positive"` | At $q = 0.8$, `{python} N.op_sparsity_08` of loadings are zero while `{python} N.op_retained_08` of the best mean linear score is retained (best $F_1$ on the $80\%$-sparse `NonnegPartsWeak` regime `{python} N.f1_npw_q08_best`). |
| Non-Linear Cross-Assay Coupling (e.g., renal cancer stage across heterogeneous assays) | `LEND` | $w = 0.50$, $q = 0.50$ | Non-linear decoders with linear input projections $\mathbf{X}_m \mathbf{V}_m$ (`TCGA-KIRC` consensus accuracy `{python} N.kirc_LEND_u_pm` vs. `{python} N.kirc_PCA_u_pm` for `PCA`). |
| Low-Dimensional Clinical Tabular Vitals ($p_m < 15$, homogeneous noise) | `NSAFlow-PCA` or `SiMLR` | $w = 0.50$, $q = 0.50$ | Exact patient-level clinical attribution ($c_{ij} = x_{ij} l_{jl}$ from OLEE loadings; `Heart` accuracy `{python} N.heart_NSAFlow_PCA` for `NSAFlow-PCA`, `Diabetes` $R^2 =$ `{python} N.diab_SiMLR` for `SiMLR`). |
| Raw Abundance / Compositional / Dietary Intake Tables (where the Perron-Frobenius global mean mode *is* the target signal) | `SiMLR` (`varimax=False`) | $w = 0.50$, `varimax=False` (`init="pca_clamp"`) | Preserves the leading all-positive global abundance/caloric mode on Component 1 rather than rotating it across all $k$ axes. |
| Sign-Oriented Directional Views or $n_m \lesssim p_m$ | `fit_uniform_shrunk` + `resolve_directional_defaults` | `positivity="auto"`, `alpha_mode="ric"`, $q \in [0.3, 0.5]$ (or `positivity="conical"` when $p_m \le 5$) | Exact column-support orthogonality ($D(\mathbf{V}_m) \le$ `{python} N.us_conical_max_defect`), Design B support recovery $F_1 =$ `{python} N.ts_b_q05_conical_ric_f1` and radial convex $R^2 =$ `{python} N.ts_b_q05_rcvx_ric_r2`, and `TCGA-BRCA` conical linear probe `{python} N.us_brca_con_lin` (@sec-uniform-shrinkage; @sec-exp-v043-revisit). |
| Subsample-Aggregated Discovery & Prediction | `bagged_fit` + `bagged_predict` | `aggregate="select"` (sparse support) or `"average"` (Procrustes-aligned refits), `n_subsamples=50`, `fraction=0.8`, `threshold=0.6` | Stabilizes high-dimensional feature supports across subsamples while `latent_stability` (`select_rank`) quantifies out-of-bag `latent_reliability` (@sec-stability-bagging-sem). |
| Downstream Pathway & Mediation Graphs | `pysimlr.path_model` vs. `observed_sem` (`observed_path_model`) | `path_model` for multi-column blocks; `observed_path_model` / `compare_observed_path_models` for single-variable Gaussian paths | Separates distribution-free permutation Pillai block tests from `observed_sem` single-variable ML SEM fit indices ($\chi^2$, RMSEA, CFI, SRMR, AIC/BIC; @sec-stability-bagging-sem; @hu1999cutoff; @steiger1990structural; @akaike1974new; @schwarz1978estimating). |

: Practitioner selection guide mapping biomedical study characteristics to recommended `SiMR` architectures and `nsa_flow` operating points. {#tbl-practitioner-guide}

## Limitations and Negative Findings

The regimes where `SiMR` architectures underperform, incur computational trade-offs, or require specific preprocessing are:

1. **No Universal Advantage Over PCA on Unaligned Single-View Unsupervised Tasks**: When a single homogeneous data matrix is analyzed without cross-modal supervision or when views share identical signal-to-noise ratios and dense Gaussian loadings, standard `PCA` maximizes variance explanation in $\mathcal{O}(\min(N p^2, p N^2))$ time (median `{python} N.pca_fit_seconds` s here). On low-dimensional clinical tables such as `Heart` ($p = [7, 6]$), `NSAFlow-PCA` reaches `{python} N.heart_NSAFlow_PCA` against `{python} N.heart_SiMLR` for multi-view `SiMLR`.
2. **Unrotated Initialization and Row-Mean Centering on Cortical Thickness**: On `ADNI-MCI`, non-negative `SiMLR` without rotation or quantile thresholding (`varimax = False, sparseness = None`) is `{python} N.fl_col_pca_simr_sp` sparse with `{python} N.fl_col_pca_simr_active` active DKT regions per component; with Varimax rotation it is `{python} N.fl_varimax_simr_sp` sparse with `{python} N.fl_varimax_simr_active`. Subject row-mean centering of the MRI views (@sec-app-operational; the cognitive outcome is not row-centered) gives `{python} N.rm_row_pca_pos_sp` sparsity and `CogPC1` $R^2 =$ `{python} N.rm_row_pca_pos_r2` (PCA start) or `{python} N.rm_row_ica_pos_r2` (ICA start), against `{python} N.rm_col_pca_pos_r2` with column centering. Sparsity alone does not make the thickness basis interpretable: at $q = 0.85$ the components keep `{python} N.fl_col_pca_q85_simr_active` regions, because the collapse penalty reduces columns on a globally correlated view to one or two regions, and the regional pattern appears only with `collapse_weight = 0` (@fig-adni-neuroanatomy-flagship D).
3. **Extreme Orthogonality Weights**: Moving the `nsa_flow` weight from $w = 0.50$ to $w = 0.95$ multiplies fit time by `{python} N.w_time_ratio_adni` on `ADNI-MCI` and `{python} N.w_time_ratio_synth` on synthetic `NonnegParts`, and changes `CogPC1` $R^2$ from `{python} N.w_r2_050` to `{python} N.w_r2_095`. At $w = 0.01$ the effective rank is `{python} N.w_effrank_001` of $k = 3$ (Gram defect $D =$ `{python} N.w_D_001`); at $w = 0.10$ it is `{python} N.w_effrank_010`. Across $w \in [0.20, 0.85]$, `CogPC1` $R^2$ stays within `{python} N.w_plateau_min`–`{python} N.w_plateau_max`.
4. **Deep Multi-View Models and Feature Support Recovery**: On the synthetic parts regimes, the deep autoencoder variants recover feature supports less well than the linear solver: $F_1 =$ `{python} N.f1_NED_np` (`NED`) and `{python} N.f1_NEDPP_np` (`NEDPP`) on `NonnegParts` against `{python} N.f1_simlr_np` for `SiMLR`, and `{python} N.f1_NED_npw` and `{python} N.f1_NEDPP_npw` on `NonnegPartsWeak` against `{python} N.f1_simlr_npw`.
5. **Dimensional Collapse vs. Correlated Factor Trade-Off (`collapse_threshold = 0.3`)**: Preventing dimensional collapse is essential in narrow or unbalanced views. The default penalty (`collapse_weight = 1.0`, `collapse_threshold = 0.3`; `docs/audit/evidence/collapse_threshold_selection.csv`) protects narrow views from collapsing into duplicate factors (at $t = 0.7$, narrow-view score correlation reaches `{python} N.collapse_t07_narrow_corr` and outcome $R^2$ changes by `{python} N.collapse_t07_narrow_r2_drop` (from `{python} N.collapse_t07_narrow_r2_base` to `{python} N.collapse_t07_narrow_r2_val`)), at the trade-off of capping recoverable score correlation between correlated latent factors near $t = 0.3$ under average mixing (`avg`: `{python} N.collapse_t03_avg_rho05` at $\rho = 0.5$ and `{python} N.collapse_t03_avg_rho07` at $\rho = 0.7$), whereas Newton polar mixing decorrelates consensus scores to `{python} N.collapse_t03_newton_max`.
6. **Unified Budgets and Optimizer Convergence Basins**: Optimization uses a unified default budget of $300$ linear sweeps and $300$ deep epochs with plateau tolerance `DEFAULT_TOL = 1e-4` (`docs/audit/evidence/default_selection_stage1.csv`, `{python} N.default_stage1_n` fits; `default_selection_stage2.csv`, `{python} N.default_stage2_n` fits with `{python} N.default_stage2_conv_rate` convergence and worst-case $R^2 =$ `{python} N.default_stage2_worst_r2`; `deep_default_consistency.csv`, `{python} N.deep_cons_n_per_family` runs per family with convergence rates `{python} N.deep_cons_conv_flow_v` for `Flow-SiMR-V`, `{python} N.deep_cons_conv_lend` for `LEND`, `{python} N.deep_cons_conv_ned` for `NED`, and `{python} N.deep_cons_conv_nedpp` for `NEDPP`). Dimensional collapse in unpenalized linear and deep fits is a step-size optimization basin rather than an objective minimum: unpenalized deep fits that collapse incur worse similarity loss than uncollapsed fits (mean `{python} N.deep_collapse_loss_collapsed`, $n =$ `{python} N.deep_collapse_n_collapsed`, versus `{python} N.deep_collapse_loss_ok`, $n =$ `{python} N.deep_collapse_n_ok`; `docs/audit/evidence/deep_collapse_diagnosis.csv`), and short-horizon step-size probes favor upper grid endpoints, motivating the 7-point probe grid spanning `1.0` to `0.001`.
7. **Scale-Free View Weighting and Standardization Invariance**: Equal view weights $\alpha_m = 1/M$ preserve scale invariance for normalized correlation and related scale-free energies, preventing view-weight spreads from muting the unweighted collapse penalty, while standardized energies (`align`, `logcosh`, `exp`, `kurtosis`, `negentropy`) use a scale-relative variance floor so rescaling any view leaves the objective invariant.
8. **Polarity User Contract and Mixed-Sign Cancellation**: `fit_uniform_shrunk` requires caller-aligned feature signs (for example via `prepare_views`); unaligned opposing signs cancel under the within-support mean projector $\Pi_m$, and non-negative constraints suppress negative loadings (@sec-uniform-shrinkage).
9. **Radial Simplex Non-Convergence on Very Low-Dimensional Views ($p_m \le 5$)**: Under $k = 2$ disjoint support extraction (`min_per_col=2`), radial simplex faces (`positivity="convex"`) failed line-search descent on `Diabetes` ($0/3$ converged, `no_descent`, consensus `{python} N.us_diab_cvx_u`, linear `{python} N.us_diab_cvx_lin`), whereas `positivity="conical"` converged in $3/3$ splits (consensus `{python} N.us_diab_con_u`, linear `{python} N.us_diab_con_lin`, $D =$ `{python} N.us_diab_con_defect`; @sec-exp-v043-revisit).
10. **Disjoint Support Assumption at $k > 1$**: In `ColumnSupportShrinkageOperator` (@eq-prop3-support-shrinkage), exact zero-defect orthogonality requires pairwise-disjoint Stage-1 lobe supports; settings requiring shared pleiotropic hubs across components at $k > 1$ should use standard `SiMLR` with `nsa_flow` ($w = 0.50$).
